newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil dips, fuel oil recovers slightly.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil dips, fuel oil recovers slightly.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Friday with gas oil slipping while fuel oil recovered marginally as some enquiries emerged from China, traders said.
Gas oil continued to be pressured by a supply overhang and was not expected to recover much despite anticipated demand from Indonesia and India, traders said.

Traders said India was expected to buy as much gas oil in its tender for March deliveries as it did for February totalling 855,000 tonnes. But they said most of the supplies would come from the MidEast and would not help alleviate the glut in Singapore. The Indian tender closes on January 23.

The market was rife with talk that a Singapore trader has at least 400,000 tonnes of gas oil in two large tankers floating off Singapore and China, but the trader said the volume was "10 times less than that."
The first bid this week was seen at $26.40 a barrel which was later raised to $27 for mid-February lifting fob.
But a major offered a mid-Feb earlier at $28.25. The major also lowered its early Feb cargo offer to $27.50.

Naphtha edged down with crude in a correction of last week's six-year highs. Feb swaps fell 55 cents to $23.80/$24.10 a barrel, in a thin market as cash and paper buyers were sidelined, awaiting lower prices. Traders expected the naphtha/gasoline spread to widen to $2.00-$2.50 a barrel on naphtha's swift fall while buyers bid up gasoline. A 97-oct unleaded cargo was bid up intraday by 20 cents to $26.80 fob for Feb 3-7 lifting. No sellers emerged despite bearish fundamentals in a well-supplied market.
